lesson.subject: numeracy
lesson.title: Perimeter
lesson.subtitle: Term 4 Week 5, Session 1
lesson.footer: Area and Perimeter | Year 5/6 Maths | Session 1

plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Number, Year 5 (VC2M5N06, VC2M5N07) applied to measurement: solving perimeter problems with efficient addition and multiplication, and checking the reasonableness of answers
plan.shape: example-first: the teacher models a rectangle, then a shape with missing sides, because finding missing sides from opposite sides is the new step
plan.criticalFeature: add every side once; a missing side comes from the opposite sides
decisionPoints: the choice check: perimeter of a 6 m by 4 m rectangle
the hinge: perimeter of an L-shape with a missing side
plan.anchor: perimeter goes around the edge (add the sides); area covers the inside (length x width)

manipulatives: A metre ruler or trundle wheel for the launch (optional)
studentTools: Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The week's anchor on the board: perimeter goes around the edge (add the sides); area covers the inside (length x width)

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. Rectangle perimeters, missing sides, a mistake to fix, and fence, oval and garden problems.
resources.title: Perimeter
resources.subtitle: Go around the edge. Add every side once.

example.prompt: Find the perimeter of a rectangle 14 m by 6 m.
steps: Add one length and one width: 14 + 6 = 20.

items.prompt: Find the missing values for each rectangle.

example.prompt: An L-shape: bottom 10, top 6, left 9, right 4. Find the two missing sides.

items.prompt: Find the missing sides, then the perimeter.
Find the missing sides, then the perimeter.

example.prompt: A pen is 20 m by 15 m. Fencing costs $10 a metre. Cost?

items.prompt: A paddock is 45 m by 28 m. Fencing costs $12 a metre. How much does it cost to fence?
A footy oval is roughly a rectangle 160 m by 130 m. Liv runs 3 laps. How far does she run?
Ava found the perimeter of a 7 cm by 5 cm rectangle. Find her mistake and fix it.
items.answer: She added only two sides. All four: 7 + 5 + 7 + 5 = 24 cm.

items.prompt: Which rectangle has the larger perimeter?
Design two different garden beds that each have a perimeter of 24 m. Sketch them and label the sides.
items.answer: Any two rectangles where length + width = 12, for example 8 m by 4 m and 10 m by 2 m.

example.prompt: A square has a perimeter of 36 cm. How long is each side?

items.prompt: A rectangle has a perimeter of 56 m. Its length is 17 m. How wide is it?
A regular hexagon has a perimeter of 72 cm. How long is each side?

example.prompt: Two 1 cm squares side by side. Perimeter?
steps: The shape is 2 cm by 1 cm.

items.prompt: Five 1 cm squares in a straight row. What is the perimeter?
Arrange four 1 cm squares to make the biggest perimeter, then the smallest. Sketch both.
items.answer: Biggest: a row of 4, perimeter 10 cm. Smallest: a 2 by 2 square, perimeter 8 cm.

example.prompt: 20 m of fence. Which rectangle pens can you make with whole metres?

items.prompt: A farmer has 24 m of fencing for a rectangular pen. Fill in the table. Which pen gives the most space inside?

slides.notes: Session 1 of our area and perimeter week: today we find the distance around shapes.
Before you start, put boards, markers and a ruler on every desk. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with last week's probability.
ASK: What is the probability of blue?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 2/6. ACCEPT: 1/3
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> count every equal part, then the blue parts. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Blue is 2 of the 6 equal parts,
so 2/6, which is 1/3. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 1/3 because there are 3 colours.
Fix: count parts, not colours, and they recount.
notes.prep: Review of Week 4 probability (the request named the focus). Keep the review under 6 minutes.

slides.title: Expected results
prompts: Roll a dice 48 times. How many sixes would you expect?

beats: ASK: How many sixes would you expect in 48 rolls?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 8
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> say the chance, one sixth, then share 48 into 6 groups. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: One sixth of 48 is 8. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 288.
Fix: say 'one sixth of', and they divide instead.

slides.title: Fraction of a survey
prompts: What fraction of students chose summer?

beats: ASK: What fraction of the students chose summer?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 12/30. ACCEPT: 2/5
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> add all the columns for the total, then put summer over it. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 12 out of 30 chose summer,
which simplifies to 2/5. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 12/18, summer over the rest.
Fix: point to the total, 30, and they rewrite it.

slides.title: Multiply with the written method: 3 digits

beats: SAY: Now for some written multiplication.
Multiply the ones first, and carry into the next column.
ASK: Use the written method to solve this one.
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 2 082
SCAN boards for the carried digits.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> model the first column together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 2 082.
Tick it or fix it, and check every step.
trap: forgetting to add the carried digit after multiplying.
Fix: write each carry small above the next column, and they redo it.
notes.prep: Multiplication fluency: 3 digits, then 4, then 5. Keep the whole block under 6 minutes.

slides.title: Multiply with the written method: 4 digits

beats: SAY: Now it's 4 digits.
It's the same method, just one more column.
ASK: Use the written method to solve this one.
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 11 424
SCAN boards for the carried digits.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> model the first column together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 11 424.
Tick it or fix it, and check every step.
trap: forgetting to add the carried digit after multiplying.
Fix: write each carry small above the next column, and they redo it.

slides.title: Multiply with the written method: 5 digits

beats: SAY: Now it's 5 digits.
It's the same method, just one more column.
ASK: Use the written method to solve this one.
60 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 95 053
SCAN boards for the carried digits.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> model the first column together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 95 053.
Tick it or fix it, and check every step.
trap: forgetting to add the carried digit after multiplying.
Fix: write each carry small above the next column, and they redo it.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to find the perimeter of rectangles and other shapes with straight sides.
successCriteria: I can find the perimeter by adding all the side lengths.
I can find missing side lengths using the opposite sides.
I can choose an efficient way to find a perimeter and explain it.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: This week is all about area and perimeter.
Today we start with perimeter: the distance around the edge.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 adding the sides is reachable for everyone; SC2 missing sides is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 an efficient method is the stretch.

slides.title: Walk the fence
slides.prompt: How far is it all the way around the fence?

beats: POINT to each side as if walking along it.
SAY: Imagine walking all the way around this garden fence, starting at a corner.
ASK: How many metres do you walk to get back to where you started?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 26 m
SCAN boards for 26.
80%+ -> cold call one student: How did you add it?
Less -> trace each side together, writing 8, 5, 8, 5. Re-ask.
SAY: It's 26 metres: 8, 5, 8 and 5.
That distance around the edge is called the perimeter.
trap: writing 13, two sides only.
Fix: walk all four sides with your finger, and they add again.
notes.prep: The launch comes after the LI: perimeter as a walk around the edge. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: The total distance around the outside of a shape.
slides.example: A 3 m by 2 m rug has a perimeter of 10 m.

beats: POINT to the word.
SAY: This word is perimeter. Say it with me: pe-rim-e-ter.
SAY: Perimeter is the total distance around the outside.
We find it by adding every side once.
ASK: Trace the perimeter of your desk with your finger. Ready, go.
5 sec. Cue: Everyone, together, on three. Trace... now.
EXPECT: fingers moving around the edge
trap: rubbing the middle of the desk.
Fix: say edge, not inside, and they trace again.
notes.prep: Perimeter is the edge; area, tomorrow, is the inside. Keep both on the anchor.

slides.title: Perimeter of a rectangle
steps: Add a length and a width: 12 + 7 = 19.

beats: POINT to the two labelled sides.
SAY: Only two sides are labelled, but opposite sides of a rectangle are equal.
So the sides are 12, 7, 12 and 7.
MODEL the efficient way.
SAY: Instead of adding four numbers, I add one length and one width, 19,
then double it: 38 metres.
ASK: What is the perimeter of a rectangle 15 metres by 9 metres?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 48 m
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 15 and 9 make 24, doubled is 48 metres.
trap: multiplying 15 by 9.
Fix: say perimeter goes around the edge, and they add instead.
notes.stretch: Find a different rectangle with the same perimeter.
notes.help: Write all four sides before you add.
notes.prep: Add a length and a width, then double. SC1 and SC3.

beats: POINT to the bottom and the top.
SAY: The bottom is 10 across and the top is 6,
so the missing across side is 10 take away 6: 4.
POINT to the left side and the right side.
SAY: The left side is 9 tall. The right part is 4,
so the missing up side is 9 take away 4: 5.
ASK: Now add all six sides. What is the perimeter?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 38 cm
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 10, 4, 4, 5, 6 and 9 make 38 centimetres.
Every side, once.
trap: leaving out the missing sides.
Fix: count the sides, six, and they add them all.
notes.stretch: Why is it the same as a 10 by 9 rectangle?
notes.help: Tick each side as you add it.
notes.prep: The critical feature: a missing side comes from the opposite sides. SC2.

slides.title: A 6 m by 4 m rectangle
slides.prompt: What is the perimeter? Point to A, B or C

options.misconception: adds only one length and one width
multiplies: finds the area, not the perimeter

beats: SAY: Think: perimeter means all the way around.
ASK: What is the perimeter of a 6 metre by 4 metre rectangle?
15 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: What did C find?
Less -> trace all four sides on a sketch together. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's B, 20 metres: 6, 4, 6 and 4.
A forgot two sides, and C multiplied, which gives the area.
trap: pointing to C.
Fix: say area covers, perimeter goes around, and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point. A: two sides only; C: perimeter confused with area.

slides.title: Find the perimeter
slides.pivot: label every side, then add them one at a time
slides.followUp: cold call one board: Which sides did you work out?

items.say: 30 metres: the missing sides are 3 and 4.

items.text: A rectangle's perimeter is 30 m. One side is 9 m. How long is the other side?
items.say: Half of 30 is 15, and 15 take away 9 is 6.

say: Write the perimeter on your board each time.
trap: missing a side.
Fix: count the sides first, and they add again.
notes.stretch: Write a quicker way for each one.
notes.help: Copy the shape and write a number on every side.
notes.prep: Guided practice: a square, a rectangle, an L-shape, then working backwards. SC1 and SC2.

beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
One side has no label. Find it first.
ASK: What is the perimeter of this shape?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 40 m
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> find the missing step together: 12 take away 7. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The missing side is 5, so 12,
5, 5, 3, 7 and 8 make 40 metres.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 35, without the missing side.
Fix: count the sides, six, and they find the missing one.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work. Anyone missing the unlabelled side starts on the Supported Worksheet with the teacher.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Find perimeters and missing sides on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: Did you add every side once?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: adding only the labelled sides.
Fix: count the sides, and they find the missing ones.
notes.stretch: Extension: working backwards, shapes from squares and the biggest pen.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: every side to label, then add, with hints.
notes.prep: Independent practice: rectangles, missing sides and real problems. The sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: What is the perimeter of the pool?

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: What is the perimeter of a pool 25 metres by 12 metres?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 74 m
RECORD who adds two sides or multiplies.
They start tomorrow's check with the teacher.
trap: writing 37 or 300.
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC1 and SC2: a new rectangle in context.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner a quick way to find a rectangle's perimeter.

notes.answer: open - listen for add a length and a width, then double it
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can find a perimeter?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with 300 on the board matters most.
ASK: What is a quick way to find a rectangle's perimeter?
20 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: add a length and a width, then double it
notes.prep: Read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence. Tomorrow: area, the inside.
